Cunning

/KUN-ing/ - the stress falls on KUN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cunning means clever in a deceptive way.

Advertisers count on a certain cunning in shelf placement, setting the sugary cereal exactly at a six-year-old's eye level.

Worked Example

The auction ring worked by cunning: one partner drove the bidding up with confident nods while the other, shabby and apparently bored, bought the real prize unnoticed.

Cunning is cleverness that has stopped being fair. A shrewd buyer simply judges well, and a clever student solves the puzzle — the cunning one solves it by arranging for you to look the other way. Deception is baked into the word.

How Cunning Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

crafty

crafty: tricky in a patient, workshop way

sly

sly: quieter and sneakier, working in the corners

Antonyms

naive

naive: trusts too easily to see the trap coming

straightforward

straightforward: says what it means and hides nothing

How Strong Is It? — clever → cunning → scheming

clever vs. cunning

clever vs. cunning: Clever is milder than cunning — clever praises the quickness of a mind and says nothing at all about honesty.

scheming vs. cunning

scheming vs. cunning: Scheming goes further than cunning: cunning may live inside a single trick, while a scheming rival runs a whole campaign of them.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cunn-

Root — cunn-: to know, to be able (Old English cunnan)

Suffix — -ing

Suffix — -ing: forming an adjective

Put it together

Put it together: Old English cunnan meant 'to know, to know how' — it is the ancestor of our plain verb can. For centuries cunning simply meant knowledgeable or skillful; then the compliment soured, and the knowing turned to trickery. The old sense survives in ken, 'the range of what one knows.'

Use the root in a new word: ken

Use the root in a new word: ken: How the ship's chronometer actually works is beyond my ken, but I can set it correctly.

Word Choice

neutral / slightly dark

Cunning is the general-purpose word for cleverness with deceit folded in. Wily, its neighbor in this unit, admires the fox a little more; guile names the talent itself. When the intelligence is honest, say shrewd or clever and keep the knife out of it.
